jobs.label: Fer
jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: premium Roblox inventory / sword-upgrade UI icon, square PNG cutout with real alpha transparency.
Input image 1: exact geometry and color reference rendered from the user's existing 3D sword; this is NOT a suggestion to redesign it.
Primary request: create a polished, vibrant, very legible game-item icon of precisely this existing weapon, using its silhouette, guard, handle, blade outline, details and colors faithfully.
Style: polished stylized 3D item render, sharp edges, attractive facet highlights, high contrast, clear readable volume; similar finish throughout the icon collection. Improve lighting, not the design.
Composition: single isolated weapon shown predominantly face-on, with a small amount of 3D depth so its broad blade face stays clearly visible. Rotate diagonally from lower LEFT pommel to upper RIGHT blade tip, roughly 40 degrees from vertical. Full tip, full guard and full pommel inside the image with safe 7% transparent margins. Large bold centered item filling most of square. For an explicitly requested dual pair use the specified X composition instead.
Background: genuinely transparent outside the weapon and its few restrained glow wisps, including gaps/holes. NO solid black or white background, NO checkerboard drawn into image, no ground or shadow plane.
Lighting: bright studio key light with crisp tasteful cool rim accents and material-appropriate specular highlights; preserve colors, never grey washed-out, never overexpose away details.
Constraints: no typography, no label, no numbers, no badge, no border, no UI card, no characters, no hands, no floor, no scenery. Do NOT invent another weapon design. No duplicate handles, no detached guard, no cut-off blade. Auras must be compact and secondary, not overpowering.
Specific subject: One broad dark iron cleaver with angled asymmetric point, two long inset panels, black wrapped grip and octagonal metal pommel. Exactly match reference. Neutral silver edge highlights; no magic aura.
